requirements.description: Annual Compustat firm-year inputs for the two H1 expected-core constructions and Table 6 outcomes/predictor: core earnings; NOA and ATO; accruals and cash flow; sales growth and its negative component; special items as a percentage of sales; native firm identity, fiscal-year and fiscal-year-end fields; and source-format/population descriptors needed to identify annual records. The source uses the 2003 Annual Compustat File and all Compustat firm-years meeting the stated H1 sample rules.

required_coverage.population: The paper’s 2003 Annual Compustat firm-year population required for H1, before and after the stated data screens; all firms with sufficient data, excluding sales below $1 million and fiscal-year-end changes between t−1/t or t/t+1, with a minimum of 15 observations per industry-fiscal-year for expected-core fitting. The precise country/population boundary of the author archive is not further specified in the passage.
required_coverage.detail: The source identifies raw data years 1988–2003 and actual analysis years 1989–2002. These annual records must supply lagged and future values for the reported measures and fiscal-year-end comparison fields; the future unexpected-change outcome and nested lagged-change/ATO predictors reach the beginning of the raw span. The current COMP.FUNDA candidate is not assumed to equal the author’s 2003 file population.

routes.source_name: Compustat North America annual fundamentals (local SAS candidate)
routes.mapping_notes: The exact local dataset and all listed columns are verified by a successful shared probe. Catalog labels provide candidate semantic fields: gvkey, datadate, fyear, fyr, sich, sale, cogs, xsga, spi, at, ch, ivst, dlc, dltt, ceq, pstk, mib, ib, oancf and xidoc, plus indfmt/consol/popsrc/datafmt. Field presence does not establish historical item correspondence or units. The mapping of current Compustat fields to the paper’s 2003 Compustat definitions remains unverified, especially the depreciation-exclusion convention for COGS/SG&A and the exact #123/#308/#124 cash-flow composition; do not map item numbers by resemblance. GVKEY is the native Compustat company key for the within-source leave-one-firm-out construction, so no external identifier link is required.
routes.coverage_notes: No coordinator-supplied local coverage confirmation exists for 1988–2003, the author’s Compustat population, or the annual sample after the stated filters. The sampled header and readable fields are not history/population confirmation.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The exact local resource and candidate columns are available, but no coordinator coverage confirmation verifies the paper’s 1988–2003 source period and 2003 Annual Compustat population. The mapping from current field definitions/vintage to the historical source item definitions and population filters is also unverified.

requirements.description: Historical Fama–French (1997) SIC-to-industry classification required to group the expected-core levels and changes regressions by industry and fiscal year, then construct leave-one-out predictions for the H1 baseline outcomes. The classification is an input to the supporting models, not an optional return or market benchmark.

required_coverage.population: All sample-company historical SIC values assigned to the industry groups used by the cited Fama and French (1997) classification.
required_coverage.detail: The paper cites Fama and French (1997), while the official current 48-industry page supplies a SIC-based definitions link and a different current assignment process. Exact historical 1997 mapping and its application to the paper’s firm-year classifications are not verified; no calendar coverage interval can be assigned to the static crosswalk.

Data are obtained for the years 1988 to 2003 from the 2003 Annual Compustat File,
I/B/E/S Split-Unadjusted File, and CRSP Daily Return Tapes. <sup>11</sup> Each firm-year observation
is required to have sufficient data to test H1. Observations with sales of less than $1 million
are deleted to avoid the creation of outliers, as sales is used as a deflator for the majority
of the variables. Also, firms that had a fiscal-year-end change from t �1 to t or from t to
t �1 are deleted to help ensure that years are comparable. Finally, I require a minimum of
15 observations per industry per fiscal year in order to ensure a sufficiently large pool to
estimate expected core earnings. Industries are classified following Fama and French
(1997);
evidence.description: Source data vintage, raw year span, sample filters, industry-year cell-size screen, and Fama–French classification. The quoted passage does not establish local data coverage.
